post.description: The core research call: pass a keyword slug from list_collection_keywords (or the keyword text / research page URL). Filter sources or cap rows per modifier to keep the response small; the related group alone can hold 2,500 rows.

keyword.description: Keyword slug from list_collection_keywords (e.g. american-airlines), the keyword text (American Airlines; lower-cased and hyphenated), or a pasted https://answerthepublic.com/{locale}/research/on/{slug} URL.

max_rows_per_modifier.description:
Keep at most this many suggestions per modifier, in the site's order (search volume descending within a modifier). Default: all rows. Coverage is reported partial when rows were dropped.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 5000.

sources.description: Return only these source groups. Default: all six.

item_id.description: ArcGIS item id of a Feature Service or Map Service (from search_datasets), optionally with a Hub `_<layer>` suffix. Alternative to url. Pattern: ^[0-9a-fA-F]{32}(_[0-9]{1,6})?$.

layer.description:
Layer id within the service, when the URL names the service only.

Provider reference: minimum 0; maximum 999999.

url.description: ArcGIS REST service or layer URL, or an ArcGIS Online item page (https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=…). https://<host>/<adaptor>/rest/services/<folder>/<service>/FeatureServer[/<layer>] or …/MapServer[/<layer>], on ArcGIS Online (services*.arcgis.com/<orgId>/arcgis/rest/services/…) or an agency's ArcGIS Server (gis.<agency>.gov/arcgis/rest/services/…). Query strings are ignored; URLs carrying a token or key are refused.

200.description:
Read an ArcGIS FeatureServer or MapServer service, or one of its layers, from its REST URL or ArcGIS item id: the service's layers and tables (id, name, type, geometry type, URL), description, capabilities and record limit; for a layer, its fields (name, alias, type, length, coded-value or range domains), geometry type, object id and display fields, extent (native and WGS84 when convertible), query capabilities and max record count. Always includes attribution: the ArcGIS Online item's licence text and credits plus the copyright text, so results can be credited. Works with ArcGIS Online (services*.arcgis.com) and any agency-hosted ArcGIS Server; the answer must be ArcGIS service JSON, otherwise invalid_input not_arcgis_service. Token-protected services are not_found.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `attribution` | object | Who to credit and the terms of use. Licence text and credits come from the ArcGIS Online item behind the service (null for agency servers without one); copyright_text from the service or layer itself. |
| `layer` | object | Layer detail when a layer was named; null for a service. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `service` | object |  |
| `url` | string | Canonical service or layer URL that was read. |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

post.description: Look up the parcel, zoning district, flood zone, permit, address point or boundary at a location or matching an id (e.g. an assessor parcel number), or page through a layer's records. Get field names from describe_layer first.

bbox.description: [west, south, east, north] in WGS84 degrees.

distance_m.description:
Search radius around point, in metres (default 0: features containing the point).

Provider reference: minimum 0; maximum 50000.

layer.description:
Layer id within the service, when the URL names the service only.

Provider reference: minimum 0; maximum 999999.

limit.description:
Rows per page; the layer's maxRecordCount may cap it lower.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 200; default 25.

offset.description:
Rows to skip (next_offset from the previous page).

Provider reference: minimum 0; maximum 100000000; default 0.

order_by.description: `FIELD` or `FIELD DESC`. Default: object id ascending, for stable paging.

out_fields.description: Fields to return (case-insensitive, checked against the layer). Default: all fields.

point.description: WGS84 point: features at (or within distance_m of) this location.

spatial_rel.description:
Relation between the features and point/bbox.

Provider reference: allowed values ["intersects", "contains", "within", "envelope_intersects"]; default "intersects".

url.description: ArcGIS REST service or layer URL: https://<host>/<adaptor>/rest/services/<folder>/<service>/FeatureServer[/<layer>] or …/MapServer[/<layer>], on ArcGIS Online (services*.arcgis.com/<orgId>/arcgis/rest/services/…) or an agency's ArcGIS Server (gis.<agency>.gov/arcgis/rest/services/…). Query strings are ignored; URLs carrying a token or key are refused.

where.description:
ArcGIS SQL-92 where clause, e.g. `PIN = '123-456-789'`, `ZONE_CODE LIKE 'R-%'`, `FLD_ZONE IN ('AE','VE')`.

Provider reference: default "1=1".

200.description:
Query one public ArcGIS feature layer or table (FeatureServer or MapServer layer that supports Query) with an ArcGIS SQL where clause, a WGS84 point (optionally with a search radius in metres) or bounding box, chosen output fields and ordering. Returns compact rows of attributes (date fields as RFC 3339 UTC) and, on request, GeoJSON geometry in WGS84 (6 decimals, vertex-capped), plus the total matching count, next_offset for paging (offset/limit up to 200 per page, respecting the layer's maxRecordCount and exceededTransferLimit) and the layer's attribution (licence, credits, copyright). count_only returns just the count. Works on ArcGIS Online and agency ArcGIS Servers; non-ArcGIS answers are invalid_input not_arcgis_service, token-protected services not_found, server-rejected clauses invalid_input rejected_by_server.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `rows` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `attributes` | object | Field name to value, as the layer defines them (dates as RFC 3339 UTC strings, text capped at 2,000 characters). |
| `geometry` | object | RFC 7946 GeoJSON geometry in WGS84 (6 decimals); null when the feature has no geometry or exceeded the vertex cap. |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

200.description:
Search the public ArcGIS Online / ArcGIS Hub catalog (www.arcgis.com portal search) for government GIS layers published as Feature Services or Map Services: parcels, zoning, flood zones, permits, addresses, boundaries and similar. Filter by keywords, one Hub open-data site (e.g. public-nps.opendata.arcgis.com, opendata.dc.gov) or ArcGIS organization id, owner and a WGS84 bounding box; sort by relevance, last modified, views or title; page through up to 10,000 results. Each item has its id, title, type, REST service URL (for describe_layer / query_layer), owner and organization, snippet, tags, dates, authoritative flag, licence and credit text, WGS84 extent and view count. Only public items are returned; there are no credentials.

The response contains the tool result directly.

post.description: Browse or rank players by 9-category stats in a public league. Pass stat_period explicitly (S_AS_2025 = 2025-26 per-game averages, S_S_2026 = 2026-27 season totals, S_AL14 = last 14 days averages, S_PS7 = next 7 days projected, S_PSR = rest of season projected). Sort by OR (pre-season rank), AR (current rank), R_PO (% rostered), MPG, NAME or a stat id (5 FG%, 8 FT%, 10 3PTM, 12 PTS, 15 REB, 16 AST, 17 ST, 18 BLK, 19 TO). For rank windows use player_rankings.

fantasy_team_id.description: Fantasy team id in this league (fteam filter). Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,3}$.

league_id.description: Public league id, the number after /nba/ in a league URL (e.g. 10000). Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,9}$.

league_url.description: A league page URL; the league id is taken from its /nba/{league_id} segment. Alternative to league_id. Pattern: ^https?://(www\.)?basketball\.fantasysports\.yahoo\.com/nba/[0-9]{1,9}(/.*)?$.

nba_team.description: NBA team filter code from the page's team dropdown (ET_2 = Boston, ET_13 = LA Lakers). Pattern: ^ET_[0-9]{1,2}$.

offset.description:
Row offset; the page serves 25 rows. Use next_offset from the previous page.

Provider reference: minimum 0; default 0.

position.description:
Position filter: P (all players), PG, SG, G, SF, PF, F, C, Util.

Provider reference: allowed values ["P", "PG", "SG", "G", "SF", "PF", "F", "C", "Util"]; default "P".

sdir.description:
Sort direction as the site encodes it (sdir).

Provider reference: allowed values ["0", "1"]; default "1".

sort.description:
Sort column as the site encodes it: OR (pre-season rank), AR (current rank), R_PO (% rostered), MPG, NAME, 0 (games played) or a stat id (5 FG%, 8 FT%, 10 3PTM, 12 PTS, 15 REB, 16 AST, 17 ST, 18 BLK, 19 TO; 4/3 FGM/FGA, 7/6 FTM/FTA). Must be one of the page's column sort keys (see columns[].sort_key). Pattern: ^([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,11}|[0-9]{1,7})$.

Provider reference: default "OR".

stat_period.description: Stat window code from the page's dropdown. Projected: S_PS7, S_PS14, S_PSR (remaining games). Totals: S_L (today), S_L7, S_L14, S_L30, S_S_{season}. Averages: S_AL7, S_AL14, S_AL30, S_AS_{season}. Standard deviation: S_SDL7, S_SDL14, S_SDL30, S_SD_{season}. {season} is the starting year (2025 = 2025-26). Omitted: the page's default (reported in stat_period). Pattern: ^S_(PS7|PS14|PSR|L|L7|L14|L30|S_[0-9]{4}|AL7|AL14|AL30|AS_[0-9]{4}|SDL7|SDL14|SDL30|SD_[0-9]{4})$.

status.description:
Availability in this league: ALL, A (available), FA (free agents), W (waivers), T (taken), K (keepers), STATE_IL (available, IL eligible). Watch list (WL) needs a login and is not supported.

Provider reference: allowed values ["ALL", "A", "FA", "W", "T", "K", "STATE_IL"]; default "ALL".

200.description:
One page (25 rows) of a public league's player list with the league's own filters: availability, position (PG/SG/G/SF/PF/F/C/Util), NBA team, fantasy team, an explicit stat window (projected next 7/14 days or rest of season; totals, averages or standard deviations for today, the last 7/14/30 days or a season), sort by a stat or rank column, and offset. Every row carries the 9-category values keyed by Yahoo stat id.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `players` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `categories` | object | The 9-category values (plus the FGM/A and FTM/A display stats) keyed by name; stat ids per stat_categories. |
| `current_rank` | number | `Current` rank column (sort AR); null when `-`. |
| `fantasy_points` | number | `Fan Pts` column, printed only in points leagues; null in category leagues or when `-`. |

fantasy_team_id.description: Fantasy team id in this league (fteam filter). Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,3}$.

offset.description:

position.description:

sdir.description:
Sort direction as the site encodes it (sdir).

Provider reference: allowed values ["0", "1"]; default "1".

sort.description:
Rank column to sort by: OR pre-season; AR_S / AR_L30 / AR_L14 / AR_L7 actual rank on total stats (season / last 30 / 14 / 7 days); AR_AS / AR_AL30 / AR_AL14 / AR_AL7 the same windows on average stats.

Provider reference: allowed values ["OR", "AR_S", "AR_L30", "AR_L14", "AR_L7", "AR_AS", "AR_AL30", "AR_AL14", "AR_AL7", "NAME"]; default "AR_S".

status.description:
Availability in this league: ALL, A (available), FA (free agents), W (waivers), T (taken), K (keepers), STATE_IL (available, IL eligible). Watch list (WL) needs a login and is not supported.

Provider reference: allowed values ["ALL", "A", "FA", "W", "T", "K", "STATE_IL"]; default "ALL".

200.description:
The full current WRO and Findings list in file order (chronological), paginated by offset with a cursor pinned to one publication (CSV URL plus SHA-256). Every page re-resolves the CSV from the dataset page and re-fetches it; if the publication moved since the cursor was issued the call fails with `invalid_input` and issue code `publication_changed` instead of mixing versions. Filters narrow the list; pass the same filters with the cursor. No `records/changes`: CBP publishes no deltas, and revoked orders drop out of the file rather than change status, so keep history by diffing snapshots.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `records` as the primary payload key.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `aliases` | string[] | Alternative names from the `Entity` column, one per ` a/k/a ` segment after the first. Empty when the entity has none. |
| `calendar_year` | number | The `Calendar Year` column as published. |
| `country` | string | The `Country` column, e.g. `Fishing Vessels` for `FV`. |
| `country_code` | string | The `Country Code` column: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, or the pseudo-code `FV` for fishing vessels. |
| `effective_date` | string | The `Effective Date` column (M/D/YYYY in the file) as an ISO date. |
| `industry` | string | The `Industry` column, or null when the file leaves it blank. `All` is a published value. |
| `manufacturer` | string | The primary name in the `Entity` column (the text before the first ` a/k/a `). Some rows name a region, a sector (`Artisanal`) or a vessel rather than a company; it is never inferred from the merchandise. |
| `merchandise` | string | The `Merchandise` column. |
| `notice_url` | string | The `Press Release` column (a CBP or Federal Register URL), or null when blank. |
| `order_type` | string | The `WRO/Finding` column: `WRO` (Withhold Release Order) or `Finding`. |
| `publication_id` | string | The CSV filename, e.g. `withhold-release-orders-findings-fy26-2026-09-29.csv`; it changes with every dataset update. |
| `raw` | object | The identity tuple exactly as published (before whitespace normalisation and alias splitting). |
| `remarks` | string | The `Remarks` column (Treasury Decision and Federal Register citations, cross-references), or null when blank. |
| `retrieved_at` | string | When this program fetched the CSV (UTC). |
| `source_record_id` | string | Derived id: `wro:` + the first 16 hex characters of SHA-256 over `Effective Date\|WRO/Finding\|Entity\|Merchandise` (whitespace in each field collapsed to single spaces). The CSV has no id column; the tuple is unique across the file. |
| `source_url` | string | The dated CSV this row was read from. |
| `status` | string | The `Status` column exactly as published (`Active`, `Partially Modified`, `Inactive-Pending Litigation`, ...). Revoked orders drop out of the file rather than change status. |

value.description:
List of issued building permits from the City of Edmonton - Urban Planning & Economy Department for the public to do construction or maintenance on a structure located in the City. Note - All records start from January 1, 2009.
Please note : the decision was made to not release applicant information on this dataset as it was seen as a potential privacy issue. For instance, if a high profile member of the public were to apply for a permit, their name (and consequently address) would show up on this table and become easily searchable by the public.  We viewed this as a potential issue and decided to publish the dataset without applicant information.

Also Note: The General Building Permits dataset now includes an "Occupancy Date" to indicate when a building has met the requirements for use or habitation. 
- Residential: Permits finalized on or after January 1, 2022.
- Non-Residential: Permits completed on or after January 1, 2024, only if an occupancy record exists.
- Historical Data: Records before these dates are blank for accuracy, or if no permit was required.
- Usage: For trend analysis only; not a legal confirmation of occupancy for property transactions.

datasets.description:
List of issued building permits from the City of Edmonton - Urban Planning & Economy Department for the public to do construction or maintenance on a structure located in the City. Note - All records start from January 1, 2009.
Please note : the decision was made to not release applicant information on this dataset as it was seen as a potential privacy issue. For instance, if a high profile member of the public were to apply for a permit, their name (and consequently address) would show up on this table and become easily searchable by the public.  We viewed this as a potential issue and decided to publish the dataset without applicant information.

Also Note: The General Building Permits dataset now includes an "Occupancy Date" to indicate when a building has met the requirements for use or habitation. 
- Residential: Permits finalized on or after January 1, 2022.
- Non-Residential: Permits completed on or after January 1, 2024, only if an occupancy record exists.
- Historical Data: Records before these dates are blank for accuracy, or if no permit was required.
- Usage: For trend analysis only; not a legal confirmation of occupancy for property transactions.

200.description:
The full current list (the batch's `records/list`), paginated with a cursor pinned to one publication. Every page re-reads the file's trailer, recomputes the publication id and compares it with the one in the cursor; when the source moved on the call fails with invalid_input whose issue code is `publication_changed` (message prefixed `publication_changed:`), never mixing publications. Pages are read as Range segments of the 34 MB consolidated.json from the pinned byte offset; on resume the last record of the previous page is re-read and its `SOURCE:id` checked against the cursor, so a re-ordered file is also reported as publication_changed. Filters: `sources` (list abbreviations; ISN is accepted for ACN), `exclude_treasury` (drops SDN, SSI, FSE, CAP, CMIC, MBS, PLC, which `sanctionssearch-ofac-treas-gov` already covers), `entity_types`, `programs` (exact program strings). A page reads until `limit` records matched or the file ended (the whole 34 MB file scans in under 10 s), so a filtered page shorter than `limit` normally means the list is exhausted; `next_cursor` is null exactly when it is. Records are grouped by source in the file (ACN first, SDN the bulk, UVL last on 2026-10-17) but no order is promised.

The response contains the tool result directly.

x-aisa-provider-response.about: The full current list (the batch's `records/list`), paginated with a cursor pinned to one publication. Every page re-reads the file's trailer, recomputes the publication id and compares it with the one in the cursor; when the source moved on the call fails with invalid_input whose issue code is `publication_changed` (message prefixed `publication_changed:`), never mixing publications. Pages are read as Range segments of the 34 MB consolidated.json from the pinned byte offset; on resume the last record of the previous page is re-read and its `SOURCE:id` checked against the cursor, so a re-ordered file is also reported as publication_changed. Filters: `sources` (list abbreviations; ISN is accepted for ACN), `exclude_treasury` (drops SDN, SSI, FSE, CAP, CMIC, MBS, PLC, which `sanctionssearch-ofac-treas-gov` already covers), `entity_types`, `programs` (exact program strings). A page reads until `limit` records matched or the file ended (the whole 34 MB file scans in under 10 s), so a filtered page shorter than `limit` normally means the list is exhausted; `next_cursor` is null exactly when it is. Records are grouped by source in the file (ACN first, SDN the bulk, UVL last on 2026-10-17) but no order is promised.

post.description: One page of observations from an EIA route (`<route>/data`) at a frequency, filtered by facet codes and a period range, sorted, with offset pagination up to 5000 rows per page. Each record carries the period, every facet as {code, name}, requested values as source strings, units copied from the source, extra source flags, and the series id when the route has one. Period formats follow the frequency (YYYY, YYYY-Qn, YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DDTHH).

api_key.description: Registered EIA API key. Omitted, the public data-browser key is discovered live (see `routes`). Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$.

cursor.description: `next_cursor` from the previous page (a row offset). Omit for the first page. Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,12}$.

data_columns.description: Data columns to return, from the route's `data_columns`. Defaults to ["value"].

end.description: Inclusive last period in the frequency's format.

facets.description: Facet filters: facet id to list of codes, e.g. {"series": ["RWTC"]} or {"stateid": ["CA"], "sectorid": ["RES"]}.

frequency.description: Frequency id from the route metadata: annual, quarterly, monthly, weekly, daily, hourly or local-hourly. Pattern: ^[a-z-]+$.

page_size.description:
Rows per page; the API caps a page at 5000 rows.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 5000; default 20.

route.description: Route path with data, such as `petroleum/pri/spt` (do not append `/data`). Pattern: ^/?[a-z0-9_-]+(/[a-z0-9_-]+)*/?$.

sort.description: Sort keys applied by the API. Defaults to newest period first.

start.description: Inclusive first period in the frequency's format.

200.description:
Text-mined annotations of one article from the Europe PMC annotations platform (SciLite): the genes and proteins, diseases, chemicals, organisms, GO terms, experimental methods and database accession numbers named in it, each grounded to a database identifier (UniProt, NCBI Taxonomy, ChEBI, GO, UMLS, EFO, PDB, ENA and others), plus gene-disease, gene-drug and disease-drug relationships (Open Targets) and gene-function statements (SIB). Entities are merged per identifier with a mention count, the matched spellings, the sections they occur in and one example in context, sorted by mentions; relationships keep the sentence that states them. value.abstract:
Introduction

The role of population-wide smoking cessation campaigns is uncertain as smoking prevalence reaches historically low levels. We examined whether the Power to Quit campaign in England, which aimed to increase uptake of evidence-based cessation support, particularly digital aids, was associated with changes in quitting behaviour.

Methods

We analysed nationally-representative cross-sectional surveys of adults in England who smoked in the past year, conducted immediately before (n=803) and after (n=1,713) the campaign (February-April 2026). Logistic regression estimated associations with quit attempts, digital cessation support, local Stop Smoking Services (SSS), and quit success, overall and by social grade. Exploratory analyses examined participants recognising campaign materials (n=799). Smoking Toolkit Study (STS) data (January 2023-June 2026; n=11,442) were used to contextualise findings against longer-term trends.

Results

In the primary pre/post analysis, there were increases in quit attempts (48.4% to 52.3%, aOR=1.16 [95%CI=0.97-1.38]), attempts involving digital support (16.0% to 18.4%, aOR=1.18 [0.92-1.50], and attempts involving SSS (2.4% to 3.6%, aOR=1.53 [0.89-2.65]), although estimates were uncertain. Associations were larger among participants recognising campaign materials (quit attempts: 64.9%, aOR=1.82 [1.47-2.26]; digital support: 28.7%, aOR=1.88 [1.44-2.45]; SSS: 5.4%, aOR=2.14 [1.19-3.88]). Increases in support uptake were particularly evident among less advantaged adults. There was no clear evidence of a change in quit success. STS data showed increases in support uptake continued from before the campaign.

Conclusions

Power to Quit coincided with increased engagement with cessation support, particularly among less advantaged adults and those recognising campaign materials. Increases in support continued pre-campaign trends, indicating that the contribution of the campaign occurred within a broader period of changing cessation behaviour.

Implications

National mass media campaigns appear to still contribute to increasing engagement with evidence-based cessation support when smoking prevalence is low, particularly among more disadvantaged groups, where smoking remains more common and quit success rates are lower. Although Power to Quit was a population-wide campaign, media planning prioritised areas with higher smoking prevalence and settings where smoking was more common and habitual, alongside sociodemographic targeting where feasible. These findings suggest that population-wide campaigns and targeted delivery strategies can be complementary rather than competing approaches.

value.abstract: Like many organisms the fungal pathogen Candida albicans senses changes in the environmental CO(2) concentration. This response involves two major proteins: adenylyl cyclase and carbonic anhydrase (CA). Here, we demonstrate that CA expression is tightly controlled by the availability of CO(2) and identify the bZIP transcription factor Rca1p as the first CO(2) regulator of CA expression in yeast. We show that Rca1p upregulates CA expression during contact with mammalian phagocytes and demonstrate that serine 124 is critical for Rca1p signaling, which occurs independently of adenylyl cyclase. ChIP-chip analysis and the identification of Rca1p orthologs in the model yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae (Cst6p) point to the broad significance of this novel pathway in fungi. By using advanced microscopy we visualize for the first time the impact of CO(2) build-up on gene expression in entire fungal populations with an exceptional level of detail. Our results present the bZIP protein Rca1p as the first fungal regulator of carbonic anhydrase, and reveal the existence of an adenylyl cyclase independent CO(2) sensing pathway in yeast. Rca1p appears to regulate cellular metabolism in response to CO(2) availability in environments as diverse as the phagosome, yeast communities or liquid culture.

Use `source: ["preprint"]` for preprints and `accession` for papers that use a given structure or dataset.

accession.description: Only articles that mention this database accession, as Europe PMC text-mines them: a PDB ID (`6VXX`), UniProt accession (`P04637`), GEO series (`GSE2034`), ENA/GenBank accession, clinical-trial ID (`NCT04368728`), DOI of a dataset and others.

cursor.description: `next_cursor` from the previous page. Repeat the same query, filters, sort and limit with it.

from_date.description: Earliest first-publication date: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}(-[0-9]{2}(-[0-9]{2})?)?$.

full_text_only.description: true: only articles whose full text `full_text` returns (open access in Europe PMC under a commercial-reuse licence).

license.description:

limit.description:

open_access.description: true: only open-access records; false: only records that are not.

query.description: Free text or Europe PMC query syntax, e.g. `furin cleavage site`, `"base editing" AND TITLE:mouse`, `AUTH:"Doudna JA"`, `GRANT_AGENCY:"Wellcome Trust"`, `MESH:"Alzheimer Disease"`. Use `*` to match everything and narrow with filters.

section.description:

to_date.description: Latest first-publication date: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}(-[0-9]{2}(-[0-9]{2})?)?$.

datasets.notes_and_known_limitations:
***Total Public Debt Outstanding Disclaimer***

There are six datasets on Fiscal Data which include the national debt, which is referred to as Total Public Debt Outstanding (TPDO). TPDO is the sum of Debt Held by the Public and Intragovernmental (Intragov) Holdings. Some datasets include debt issued by the Federal Financing Bank (FFB). The datasets listed below only include debt issued by the Treasury Department. The list below provides information on where there are differences in debt calculations related to the national debt.

Debt to the Penny contains TPDO, as well as a breakout of Debt Held by the Public and Intragov Holdings. In this dataset, Intragov Holdings includes debt issued by the FFB.

Historical Debt Outstanding contains TPDO, but no breakout of Debt Held by the Public and Intragov Holdings. In this dataset, TPDO includes debt issued by the FFB.

Daily Treasury Statement (DTS) contains Debt Held by the Public and Intragov Holdings, but does not aggregate these two categories into TPDO. In this dataset, Intragov Holdings includes debt issued by the FFB. Dollar values for Debt Held by the Public and Intragov Holdings are rounded in millions to cohere with other data in the dataset. Please note that the published reports on the Fiscal Service site contain TPDO values.

Monthly Treasury Statement (MTS) contains TPDO, as well as a breakout of Debt Held by the Public and Intragov Holdings. In this dataset, Intragov Holdings includes debt issued by the FFB.

Monthly Statement of the Public Debt (MSPD) contains TPDO, as well as a breakout of Debt Held by the Public and Intragov Holdings. In this dataset, Intragov Holdings includes debt issued by the FFB. Dollar values are rounded in millions to cohere with other data in the dataset.

Schedules of Federal Debt contains Debt Held by the Public and Intragov Holdings, but does not aggregate these two categories into TPDO. In this dataset, Intragov Holdings do not include debt issued by the FFB. Dollar values are rounded in millions to cohere with other data in the dataset.

***End Total Public Debt Outstanding Disclaimer***

Debt broken out by intragovernmental holdings and debt held by the public has not always been provided. Where this occurred, the dataset shows a value of $0.00 instead of a null value. Debt held by the public and intragovernmental holdings data is available yearly (on a fiscal basis) from 9/30/1997 through 9/30/2001, monthly from 9/30/2001 through 3/31/2005, and daily from 4/4/2005 to today. Some columns in this dataset overlap with the [Monthly Statement of the Public Debt (MSPD)](https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/datasets/monthly-statement-public-debt/), [Monthly Treasury Statement (MTS)](https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/datasets/monthly-treasury-statement/), [Daily Treasury Statement (DTS)](https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/datasets/daily-treasury-statement/), and [Schedules of Federal Debt](https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/datasets/schedules-federal-debt/) datasets. Debt issued by the Federal Financing Bank (FFB) is included in the intragovernmental holdings in the Debt to the Penny dataset, but not in the Schedules of Federal Debt dataset because it is not debt managed by the Bureau of the Fiscal Service. The difference between these datasets is equal to the amount of debt issued by the FFB.

Downloaded CSV files with values greater than $10 trillion may have the final two digits (cents) excluded due to digit limits enforced by the application used to access the file. The JSON and XML file downloads are not impacted by this limitation.

Total Public Debt Outstanding = Debt Held by the Public + Intragovernmental Holdings

Please note that Total Public Debt Outstanding may be calculated differently within different datasets. See those datasets Notes & Known Limitations section for calculation details.

200.description:
Cheap version check of the USA Structures publication. Reads the hub downloads page (portal item data) for the current state zip link of every state and territory (56 rows; the bucket listing omits current files, so the page is authoritative), HEADs each zip on the public S3 bucket for size, ETag (multipart MD5, the publisher's only posted hash), x-amz-version-id and Last-Modified, derives the release date from the file name (PR_Structures_20260913 -> 2026-09-13; Deliverable20250606TX -> 2025-06-06), and reports the hosted view's dataLastEditDate as the records publication id. With `state` set, adds the view's row count for that state; with `include_fgdc` (one state only) two or three S3 range reads parse the zip central directory and the embedded FGDC metadata XML (publication date, imagery date range, access and use constraints). Every state file exceeds the 32 MiB fetch cap (only the small territories AS, GU, MP, VI and DC fit), so `handoff` is true for them: download the file_url out of band and use records_list for rows.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `states` as the primary payload key.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `content_hash` | object |  |
| `content_type` | string |  |
| `etag` | string | S3 ETag without quotes; multipart uploads carry a -N suffix. |
| `fgdc` | object |  |
| `file_name` | string |  |
| `file_url` | string |  |
| `handoff` | boolean | true when the file exceeds the 32 MiB runner cap (every state; false only for the small territories AS, GU, MP, VI and DC). |
| `hub_table_name` | string | The state name as written in the hub table row. |
| `last_modified` | string | RFC 3339 UTC from the Last-Modified header. |
| `last_modified_raw` | string |  |
| `naming` | string | structures = {ST}_Structures_{YYYYMMDD} (2026 refresh); deliverable = Deliverable{YYYYMMDD}{ST} (2025 deliverables). |
| `publication_id` | string | File stem, e.g. PR_Structures_20260913 or Deliverable20250606TX. |
| `release_date` | string | YYYYMMDD from the file name. |
| `size_bytes` | number |  |
| `state` | string |  |

| `state_name` | string |  |

| `view_record_count` | number | Rows in the hosted view with this STATE_FIPS; only when one state was requested. The view is an older vintage than the 2026 files. |

records.description:
The Rural Utilities Service (RUS or the Agency), a Rural Development (RD) agency of the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), is soliciting Letters of Interest (LOI) for applications under the Affordable Rural Cooperative (ARC) Program. In addition, the Agency is announcing the eligibility requirements, application process and deadlines, and the criteria that will be used by RUS to assess ARC Applications. The ARC Program is making approximately $175 million in appropriated budget authority for the cost of loan and grant funds available under the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) of 2022. In keeping with the statutory authority for the program, RUS will utilize the ARC funds to assist Eligible Entities to achieve future net reductions consistent with Section 22004 of the IRA through the deployment of advanced, efficient transmission infrastructure and nuclear power supply. Available funds will be allocated for each purpose while advancing the long-term resiliency, reliability, and affordability of rural electric systems. All Eligible Entities are responsible for any expenses incurred in developing their LOIs and ARC Applications.


This funding notice advances the statutory purpose of achieving the greatest reductions as provided in Section 22004 of the IRA associated with rural electric systems by increasing the amount of emission-free nuclear power and increasing the efficiency of the transmission grid within such systems. These new sources of cooperative power supply and enhanced transmission efficiency will result in reduced future demand for other sources of power.


Cost Sharing or Matching:

For Project and System loans, RUS will finance up to 75 percent of the total capitalized cost of the Project in the loan component of a Project and/or System Award. The Awardee will be required to initially provide and maintain for the term of the Project and/or System Award at least 25 percent of the Project’s total capitalized cost in the form of cash or an equity investment.


As noted in Section 2.0 of the NOFO, the Agency may where Financially Feasible allow an Awardee to utilize the grant component of the Award and/or any applicable tax credit that it expects to receive (including credit amounts expected to be received through Elective Pay elections under section 6417 of the Internal Revenue Code) toward the 25 percent equity requirement for a Project Award. Such financial equity may not come from the proceeds of any loan from any creditor, including insiders of the Awardee.

post.description: Search Grants.gov funding opportunities by keyword, agency, status, eligibility, funding category, assistance listing and posted-date window; one page of summary records (or full records with expand).

agency_ids.description: Grants.gov agency codes (e.g. HHS-NIH11, NSF, USDA-RUS). Department-level codes without a hyphen (e.g. HHS, DOD) are expanded to all sub-agencies using one extra facet request. Use `facets` to list codes.

cursor.description: next_cursor from a previous response with the same filters. Cursors from a different filter set, malformed cursors, or cursors beyond depth 10000 are rejected with invalid_input.

eligibilities.description: Two-digit Grants.gov applicant eligibility codes, e.g. 00 State governments, 01 County governments, 02 City or township governments, 04 Special district governments, 05 Independent school districts, 06 Public and State controlled institutions of higher education, 07 Native American tribal governments (Federally recognized), 08 Public housing authorities/Indian housing authorities, 11 Native American tribal organizations (other than Federally recognized), 12 Nonprofits having a 501(c)(3) status, 13 Nonprofits without 501(c)(3), 20 Private institutions of higher education, 21 Individuals, 22 For profit organizations other than small businesses, 23 Small businesses, 25 Others, 99 Unrestricted. Any code matches (OR).

expand.description: Fetch the full detail record for every hit (one extra upstream request each; requires page_size <= 20).

funding_categories.description: Grants.gov funding activity category codes, e.g. AG Agriculture, AR Arts, BC Business and Commerce, CD Community Development, CP Consumer Protection, DPR Disaster Prevention and Relief, ED Education, ELT Employment/Labor/Training, EN Energy, ENV Environment, FN Food and Nutrition, HL Health, HO Housing, HU Humanities, ISS Income Security and Social Services, IS Information and Statistics, LJL Law/Justice/Legal Services, NR Natural Resources, RA Recovery Act, RD Regional Development, ST Science and Technology, T Transportation, O Other. Any code matches (OR). Use `facets` for the live list.

funding_instruments.description: G Grant, CA Cooperative Agreement, PC Procurement Contract, O Other.

opportunity_number.description: Exact-ish funding opportunity number filter (source oppNum).

page_size.description:
page_size

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 100; default 20.

published_from.description: Earliest posted date (inclusive), YYYY-MM-DD. The source has no date filter, so a window forces posted_desc sort and scans up to 5 upstream pages (500 records) per call, resuming via next_cursor. Pattern: ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$.

published_to.description: Latest posted date (inclusive), YYYY-MM-DD. Must not be earlier than published_from. Pattern: ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$.

query.description:
Keyword(s) matched by Grants.gov full-text search over title, number, description and agency. Separate words are matched with OR (`community solar` returns every notice mentioning either word); wrap a multi-word concept in double quotes (`"community solar"`) for an exact-phrase match. A multi-term query adds a warning saying so. Empty = browse.

Provider reference: default "".

sort.description:
Ordering. A publication-date window requires posted_desc.

Provider reference: allowed values ["relevance", "posted_desc", "posted_asc", "close_asc", "close_desc"]; default "posted_desc".

statuses.description: Normalized status. posted = open for applications (source `posted`); forecast = planned, not yet open (source `forecasted`); closed = deadline passed, still listed (source `closed`); archived = removed from the public search after its archive date (source `archived`). Default posted+forecast; add closed/archived explicitly.

post.description: Discover projects before fetching one with get_project. Use list_categories for category ids and search_locations for woe_ids.

category_id.description:
Numeric category id from list_categories or a card's `category.id` (e.g. 34 = Tabletop Games, 12 = Games).

Provider reference: minimum 1.

cursor.description: `next_cursor` from a previous page (`seed:page`). Mutually exclusive with `page` and `seed`. Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,12}:[0-9]{1,3}$.

goal.description:
Goal bucket 0..5 as on the discover page (0 = under $1,000 ... 5 = over $100,000).

Provider reference: minimum 0; maximum 5.

page.description:
1-based page; 12 cards per page. Kickstarter answers 404 past roughly page 200.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 200; default 1.

raised.description:
Funding bucket: 0 = under 75% funded, 1 = 75%-100%, 2 = over 100%.

Provider reference: minimum 0; maximum 2.

recommended.description: Only projects Kickstarter marks as recommended.

seed.description:
Shuffle seed returned by a previous page; keeps `magic` order stable while paginating.

Provider reference: minimum 0.

sort.description:
Kickstarter sort. `magic` is a seeded shuffle: pass the returned `seed` (or `cursor`) to keep the order across pages.

Provider reference: allowed values ["magic", "newest", "popularity", "most_funded", "end_date", "most_backed"]; default "magic".

state.description:
Limit to live campaigns or to successfully funded ones. Omit for Kickstarter's default mix.

Provider reference: allowed values ["live", "successful"].

tag.description: Browse a tag collection (/discover/tags/{tag}, e.g. `witchstarter`, `make-100`; slugs from list_categories.tags). Combines with `sort` and `page` only. Pattern: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,80}$.

woe_id.description:
Location WOE id from search_locations (e.g. 2357536 = Austin, TX).

Provider reference: minimum 1.

An unknown term yields `total_hits: 0` and an empty `projects` array.

| `page` | number |  |

| `term_categories` | object[] | Categories Kickstarter associates with a free-text term (empty for browse queries). |
| `total_hits` | number | Kickstarter's total match count for the query. |

200.description:
Kickstarter search-box suggestions (GET /projects/search.json?term=): the project cards Kickstarter proposes for a typed term, in every state (live, successful, canceled, ...), in one response without pagination. Same card shape as search_projects. The suggestion endpoint takes only a term and has no page or cursor: has_more and total_hits only say the term matches more projects than the suggestion box shows. To see them, call search_projects with the same term and page through it (page, next_cursor).

The response contains the tool result directly.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | number | Number of cards in this response. |
| `has_more` | boolean | Kickstarter's own flag that the term matches more projects than the suggestion set returned here. This endpoint cannot be paged: use search_projects with the same term (page / next_cursor) to retrieve the rest, or add words to the term to narrow the suggestions. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number | Milliseconds since the Unix epoch when this result was fetched. |
| `projects` | object[] | Project cards in the order Kickstarter returned them. |
| `ref_tag` | string |  |

| `term` | string |  |
| `term_categories` | object[] |  |

An address the site will not deliver to returns `fee_status: not_deliverable` with null fees.

location_number.description:
Optional store number (locationNumber from search_stores). When omitted, the store the order app would assign to this address is used. Unknown store -> not_found.

Provider reference: minimum 1.

state.description: Two-letter province or territory code (ON, QC, BC, ...). Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{2}$.

street.description: Street address line, e.g. 1010 Gerrard St E. Delivery fees are quoted per address.

zip.description: Canadian postal code, with or without the space (M4M 1Z3). Pattern: ^[A-Za-z][0-9][A-Za-z] ?[0-9][A-Za-z][0-9]$.

200.description:
Delivery fee quote for a Canadian street address (POST /api/v1/store/{n}/can-deliver, the order app's delivery eligibility check): the delivery fee, service fee rate, small order fee and its threshold, minimum order and estimated delivery time. Without `location_number` the delivering store is resolved first (POST /api/v1/search/find-delivery-store). No cart, order or payment is created. An address the site will not deliver to returns `fee_status: not_deliverable` with null fees.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `address_validated` | boolean | True when the site accepted the address for delivery. |
| `currency` | string |  |
| `delivery_address` | object | The address that was quoted, as sent. |
| `delivery_fee` | number | Courier delivery fee in CAD (deliveryFees.vendorFee). Null when no fee is published or the address is not deliverable. |
| `estimated_delivery_time` | string | Delivery estimate as the site words it, e.g. 33-38 min. |
| `fee_status` | string | available: a fee was quoted. not_published: the store accepted the address but returned no fee. not_deliverable: no store delivers to the address. |
| `lce_delivery_fee` | number | Additional Little Caesars delivery fee component (lceDeliveryFee), 0 when none. |
| `location_number` | number | Store that quoted the fee; null when no store delivers to the address. |
| `minimum_order_amount` | number | Minimum delivery subtotal (minimumDeliveryThreshold), 0 when none. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number | Milliseconds since the Unix epoch when this result was fetched. |
| `quote_type` | string |  |
| `service_fee_rate` | number | Service fee as a fraction of the order subtotal (lceServiceFee, 0.12 = 12%). |
| `small_order_fee` | number | Fee added to orders under small_order_fee_threshold, unless a promotion waives it. |
| `small_order_fee_threshold` | number | Subtotal under which the small order fee applies. |
| `source` | string | The endpoint that answered. |
| `status_message` | string | The site's message when the address is not deliverable. |
| `store_source` | string | Whether the store came from the input or was resolved from the address. |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

post.description: Discovery: find products by keyword or browse a category (e.g. "Graphics Cards|518") for a given store_id. Use lookup_by_sku for a known SKU and get_product for full details.

category.description: Category facet as the site writes it in fq=category:{Name}|{id}, e.g. "Graphics Cards|518" or "Computer Parts|94".

in_store_only.description: true (default): only items in stock at store_id (myStore=true). false: include out-of-stock and not-carried items.

page.description:
1-based page; default 1. Use next_page from the previous call.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 500.

per_page.description:
Results per page; default 24.

Provider reference: allowed values ["24", "48", "96"].

query.description: Keyword search (Ntt). Optional when category is given.

sort.description:
Sort order; default match.

Provider reference: allowed values ["match", "pricelow", "pricehigh", "rating", "numreviews", "newest"].

store_id.description: 3-digit zero-padded store number (045 St. Louis Park, 205 Phoenix, 141 Columbus). Default 029 = Shippable Items (web pricing, no store inventory). list_stores returns the ids. Pattern: ^[0-9]{3}$.

200.description:
Read one Workday posting through the career site's CXS job API: title, requisition id, full description (text and HTML), primary and additional locations, country, time type, remote type, posting dates, apply URL and hiring entity.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `additional_locations` | string[] | Further locations of a multi-location posting; empty when there are none. |
| `apply_url` | string | The posting's Workday apply page. |
| `attribution` | string | Source attribution. |
| `can_apply` | boolean | Whether Workday accepts applications for the posting. |
| `career_site` | object | The Workday career site the call addressed, parsed from the input URL. |
| `country` | object | Country of the primary location; null when Workday omits it. |
| `description_html` | string | Full description HTML as Workday serves it. |
| `description_text` | string | Full description as plain text with line breaks. |
| `external_path` | string | Canonical posting path /job/{location}/{posting}. |
| `hiring_organization` | string | Hiring legal entity as Workday names it. |
| `job_posting_id` | string | Workday posting id (the last external_path segment). |
| `location` | string | Primary location. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number | When the source was read (Unix ms). |
| `posted_date` | string | Posting start date (YYYY-MM-DD), Workday startDate. |
| `posted_on_text` | string | Relative posting text, e.g. 'Posted 30+ Days Ago'. |

Job Description:

At Bank of America, we are guided by a common purpose to help make financial lives better through the power of every connection. Responsible Growth is how we run our company and how we deliver for our clients, teammates, communities and shareholders every day.

One of the keys to driving Responsible Growth is being a great place to work for our teammates around the world. We’re devoted to being a diverse and inclusive workplace for everyone. We hire individuals with a broad range of backgrounds and experiences and invest heavily in our teammates and their families by offering competitive benefits to support their physical, emotional, and financial well-being.

Bank of America believes both in the importance of working together and offering flexibility to our employees. We use a multi-faceted approach for flexibility, depending on the various roles in our organization.

Working at Bank of America will give you a great career with opportunities to learn, grow and make an impact, along with the power to make a difference. Join us!

Job Description:
This job is responsible for providing comprehensive advice and customized solutions to clients to help them achieve their financial goals. Key responsibilities include triaging client leads, making referrals to business partners based on client needs and asset thresholds, meeting with clients to review financial and investment goals, building a financial plan, and recommending brokerage products. Job expectations include applying and expanding knowledge by completing required licenses and trainings. This position is subject to SAFE Act registration requirements. Pursuant to the SAFE Act requirements, all employees engaged in residential loan mortgage originations must register with the federal registry system and remain in good standing. Since this position requires SAFE Act registration, employees are required to register and to submit to the required SAFE Act background check and registration process. Failure to obtain and/or maintain SAFE Act registration may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination.

Responsibilities:

  • Works with clients to plan their short and long-term financial goals by building a financial plan with brokerage products, including stocks, bonds, mutual funds, annuities, and banking and money managed solutions
  • Recommends banking and investments strategies that align with client financial goals and needs
  • Triages client requests and makes referrals to appropriate internal service providers based on client needs and asset thresholds
  • Mitigates and controls risk as part of daily activities
  • Identifies and engages potential new clients through referrals or financial center clientele
  • Provides coaching and feedback to referral partners based on knowledge of client needs and potential product services recommended

Skills:

  • Account Management
  • Advisory
  • Client Experience Branding
  • Customer and Client Focus
  • Oral Communications
  • Active Listening
  • Attention to Detail
  • Client Solutions Advisory
  • Issue Management
  • Pipeline Management
  • Causation Analysis
  • Client Management
  • Policies, Procedures, and Guidelines
  • Risk Management
  • Written Communications

Minimum Education Requirement: High School Diploma / GED / Secondary School or equivalent

Shift:

1st shift (United States of America)

Hours Per Week: 

40

Pay Transparency details

US - WA - Mercer Island - 2830 80th Ave Se - MERCER ISLAND BC (WA3143)

Pay and benefits information

Pay range

$70,000.00 - $80,000.00 annualized salary, offers to be determined based on experience, education and skill set.

Formulaic incentive eligible

This role is eligible to participate in a formulaic incentive plan. Employees are eligible for incentives as detailed by the specific line of business incentive plan provisions. Formulaic plans may be comprised of monthly, quarterly and/or annual incentive opportunities. Incentives are earned based on the employee’s performance against defined metrics.

Benefits

This role is currently benefits eligible. We provide industry-leading benefits, access to paid time off, resources and support to our employees so they can make a genuine impact and contribute to the sustainable growth of our business and the communities we serve.

post.description: Start here with any Workday career-site URL. Read `facets` to filter by location, job category, time type or remote type (parameters differ per employer), page with next_offset, then call get_job with a result's external_path or url for the full description.

career_site.description: Any URL of a Workday career site: https://{tenant}.wd{N}.myworkdayjobs.com/{site} (an /en-US/-style locale segment, a search-results URL with ?q= and facet parameters, or a posting URL are fine) or https://wd{N}.myworkdaysite.com/recruiting/{tenant}/{site}.

facets.description: Filters as Workday exposes them: each {parameter, ids} uses a facet parameter and value ids from a previous search_jobs `facets`. Values within one parameter are ORed, parameters are ANDed. When omitted, facet parameters in a pasted search-results URL apply.

limit.description:
Results per page; Workday serves at most 20.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 20; default 20.

offset.description:
Result offset: 0 for the first page, then the previous page's next_offset. Workday serves only the first 2000 results of a query.

Provider reference: minimum 0; maximum 1999; default 0.

query.description: Keyword search over the site's postings (Workday searchText). Omit to list everything. When omitted, a pasted URL's ?q= applies.

season_type.description: Season type: PRE, REG or POST (case-insensitive). Defaults to the current calendar phase, REG for other seasons. Pattern: ^([Pp][Rr][Ee]|[Rr][Ee][Gg]|[Pp][Oo][Ss][Tt])$.

team.description: Club UUID (e.g. 10400200-f401-4e53-5175-0974e4f16cf7) or NFL abbreviation (ATL, AZ, KC, LAR, LV, WAS...). Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$.

week.description:
Week number. Defaults to the current league week (required when `season` is not the current season).

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 30.

200.description:
Geocode a free-text query (`query`) or a structured address (`street`, `city`, `county`, `state`, `country`, `postalcode`) with Nominatim (`GET nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search`, format jsonv2, addressdetails and extratags on). Returns places with their OSM type and id, coordinates, category/type, address breakdown and bounding box; with `polygon: true` also the boundary GeoJSON, so a city or neighbourhood polygon can feed `search_elements`. Continues with `continuation` (Nominatim `exclude_place_ids`).

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `results` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | object | Nominatim address breakdown (house_number, road, suburb, city, state, postcode, country, country_code, ISO3166-2-lvl*, ...); null when not requested. |
| `addresstype` | string |  |
| `boundingbox` | object | Bounding box in decimal degrees (Nominatim order south,north,west,east, parsed to numbers). |
| `category` | string | OSM tag key that classifies the place (e.g. boundary, place, amenity). |
| `display_name` | string |  |
| `extratags` | object | Extra OSM tags Nominatim keeps (wikidata, website, population, ...); null when absent or not requested. |
| `geojson` | object | GeoJSON geometry of the place (Point, LineString, Polygon or MultiPolygon) when `polygon` was requested; null otherwise. |
| `importance` | number |  |
| `lat` | number |  |
| `lon` | number |  |
| `name` | string | Place name; empty string when the object is unnamed. |
| `osm_id` | number |  |
| `osm_type` | string | node, way or relation; null for the rare place without an OSM object. |
| `place_id` | number | Nominatim-internal id; not stable across reimports, do not persist it as a key. |
| `place_rank` | number |  |
| `type` | string | OSM tag value for `category` (e.g. administrative, city, restaurant). |
| `url` | string | https://www.openstreetmap.org/{osm_type}/{osm_id}; null when no OSM object. |

post.description: Screening and prospect lists of French companies: e.g. software publishers (58.29C) or IT consultancies (62.02A) in Île-de-France with 50-249 employees and over EUR 10M revenue, manufacturers whose executive is 60+ (succession targets), ESS structures in a department, or finding a company's SIREN from its name. commune_codes.description: INSEE commune codes (5 characters, e.g. 75056 Paris, 2A004 Ajaccio); matches units with an establishment there.

company_categories.description: INSEE company category: PME (SME), ETI (mid-cap), GE (large enterprise).

departments.description: Department codes (01-95, 2A, 2B, 971-976); matches units with an establishment there.

labels.description: Only units carrying all these public labels: ess (social and solidarity economy), sole_proprietorship (entreprise individuelle), association, local_authority (collectivité territoriale), mission_company (société à mission), public_administration, rge (RGE environmental certification), qualiopi (training quality), organic (Agence Bio), training_organization, siae (work-integration structure), finess (health/social facility), living_heritage (Entreprise du Patrimoine Vivant), entertainment_contractor (licence d'entrepreneur de spectacles), responsible_purchasing (RFAR label), alim_confiance (food-safety inspection published), uai (education establishment), egapro (gender pay-equality index published), collective_agreement (collective agreement IDCC on file).

naf_codes.description: Main activity of the legal unit, NAF rév. 2 / APE codes such as 62.01Z (6201Z accepted). Any of them matches.

net_income_max.description: Maximum net income of the latest published accounts, euros.

net_income_min.description: Minimum net income (résultat net) of the latest published accounts, euros (negative allowed).

person_birth_date_max.description: Latest birth date of an executive or elected official (YYYY-MM). For 'executive aged 60+' in October 2026, pass 1966-10. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])(-[0-9]{2})?$.

person_birth_date_min.description: Earliest birth date of an executive or elected official (YYYY-MM; a day is accepted and ignored). For 'executive under 40' in 2026, pass 1986-11. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])(-[0-9]{2})?$.

person_last_name.description: Last name of an executive (dirigeant) or local elected official.

person_type.description:

postal_codes.description: Postal codes; matches legal units with at least one establishment there.

200.description:
Search French legal units (unités légales) in Sirene + RNE by name, address, executive name or SIREN/SIRET, and/or filter by NAF activity code or section, salaried headcount band, INSEE category (PME/ETI/GE), legal form, postal code, commune, department, region, active/ceased status, public labels (ESS, sole proprietorship, association, RGE, Qualiopi, mission company...), latest revenue and net-income ranges, and executive or elected-official name and birth-date range. Each result is the full company record (legal form, NAF code and label, headcount band decoded to a range, category, creation date, status, head office with address and coordinates, executives, latest published revenue and net income, establishment counts, VAT numbers, labels) plus the establishments that matched the query. 10 per page by default (25 max), `next_page` continues; the API serves at most 10,000 results per query.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `results` as the primary payload key.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `acronym` | string | Acronym (sigle). |
| `activity` | object | Main activity; null when not published. |
| `association_id` | string | RNA association identifier, for associations. |
| `category` | object | INSEE company size category (catégorie d'entreprise); null when not computed. |
| `ceased_on` | string | Cessation date (YYYY-MM-DD) for a ceased unit. |
| `created_on` | string | Creation date of the legal unit (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `diffusion_status` | string | Sirene diffusion status: O = public, P = partially public (some personal fields withheld at the person's request). |
| `establishments_count` | number | Number of establishments, open and closed. |
| `executives` | object[] | Executives (dirigeants) as published by the RNE / Sirene sources, in source order. Not enriched. |
| `finances` | object[] | Published annual accounts figures, newest year first; empty when none are published (accounts confidential, not filed, or not yet loaded). |
| `head_office` | object | Head office (siège) establishment; null for units without a Sirene establishment. |
| `headcount` | object | Salaried headcount band as published by INSEE Sirene; null when Sirene publishes none. |
| `labels` | string[] | Public labels and registers the unit belongs to (same names as the search `labels` filter). |
| `legal_form` | object | Legal form; null when not published. |
| `legal_name` | string | Registered legal name (raison sociale) for a legal person. |
| `matching_establishments` | object[] | Establishments that matched the query text or location filters (up to 10); empty for a plain SIREN or filter-only match. |
| `name` | string | Display name composed by the API (legal name, trade name and acronym in parentheses; first and last name for a sole proprietor). |
| `open_establishments_count` | number | Number of open establishments. |
| `siren` | string | SIREN, the 9-digit legal-unit identifier. |
| `status` | string | Sirene administrative state of the legal unit; null for RNE-only units without a Sirene record. |
| `updated_at` | string | Last update of the unit in the API index (ISO 8601). |
| `vat_numbers` | string[] | Active French intra-community VAT numbers (DGFiP). |

post.description: Start here to find products by name or brand, to list a category, or to enumerate the catalogue page by page; then call get_product with a returned upc for the record with its related items.

category_id.description: Category public id (uuid) as returned by list_categories (`id`) or seen in the site's `/products?category=` links. Includes the category's descendants. Pattern: ^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$.

page.description:
1-based page of 42 products; pass the returned next_cursor to continue.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 1000; default 1.

query.description:
Free-text search (product description or brand, e.g. `advil`). Empty or omitted lists the catalogue.

Provider reference: default "".

sort.description:
Sort order; the site's own values.

Provider reference: allowed values ["description", "price_asc", "price_desc"]; default "description".

special_offers_only.description: Only products in the site's 'On Sale' view (`/products?special=true`); their `price_override` carries the sale price.

wholesale_prices.description: Return wholesale unit prices instead of retail ones, as the public 'Wholesale Prices' toggle on the site does (no login involved).

200.description:
Search or browse the Russelco catalogue through the storefront's own listing server action (POST /products, Next.js `loadMoreProducts`): free-text query, category filter (category public id from list_categories), sort (description | price_asc | price_desc), the 'On Sale' view (special_offers_only) and the public 'Wholesale Prices' toggle (wholesale_prices). Returns one page of up to 42 products with UPC, description, unit price, sale price (price_override), case pack, quantity on hand, status and image URL, plus the site's total count and page count. With no query and no filters it pages through the whole catalogue (sorted by description). A query with no matches is a successful empty page.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `category_id` | string | The category public id filtered on, null when none. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `paging` | object |  |
| `products` | object[] |  |
| `query` | string | The query as sent (trimmed). |
| `sort` | string |  |
| `source_url` | string | The public listing or search page for these filters (the page number is not part of the site's URLs). |
| `special_offers_only` | boolean |  |
| `wholesale_prices` | boolean | True when `price` and `price_override` are the site's wholesale unit prices. |

Search the Socrata catalog for datasets, across every public Socrata portal in a region or limited to one portal (`domain`), by free text, category and tags, paged with limit/offset (up to 100 per page). Each dataset has its 4x4 id, name, owning portal domain, plain-text description, category, tags, attribution, license, created/updated dates, the column field names and types, popularity, permalink and SODA API URL. A domain that no Socrata region serves fails with invalid_input not_socrata_portal; a search with no matches is a successful empty result.

products.description:
The Jordan 4 Retro London gives the AJ4 a look shaped by the city in its name. Dark Smoke Grey suede and textured overlays create a worn, concrete inspired appearance, with Hemp and Red Bark bringing earthy contrast. The darker palette keeps the shoe restrained from a distance, but its materials and small details make it rewarding to examine up close.

London references appear throughout the release. Nike LDN branding marks the heel tab and hangtag, while an upside down "SAY LESS" tag sits beneath the tongue. Red Bark laces are also included, giving collectors another way to wear the pair while keeping its original accessories together. The release was presented as a UK and European exclusive, making its regional identity central to the design rather than simply a nickname.

For AJ4 collectors, this pair offers a specific city story through color, texture, and branding. Those details give it a distinct place beside more widely released Jordan 4s. The Jordan 4 Retro London released September 12, 2026, with a retail price of $230.
products.title: Jordan 4 Retro London

products.description:
The Air Jordan 9 Retro OG Space Jam 2026 revives one of the most beloved and culturally significant colorways in Jordan Brand history, combining white, true red, and black to honor the original silhouette's connection to the beloved Space Jam film. Michael Jordan's Space Jam appearance remains one of the most iconic crossovers between basketball and Hollywood entertainment, giving this colorway genuine cinematic and cultural significance beyond a standard sneaker release. The OG designation reflects a faithful return to the exact color story and construction associated with this legendary release.

Space Jam holds a special place within both basketball and film history, representing a genuinely unique crossover moment that introduced Michael Jordan's legacy to audiences well beyond traditional basketball fandom. This white, true red, and black combination has become deeply embedded within Jordan Brand's storytelling, consistently ranking among the most celebrated and nostalgic color stories the Jordan 9 has ever produced. Collectors who appreciate both basketball history and this iconic film crossover find this Space Jam release a genuinely significant way to own a piece of this legendary cultural moment.

The Air Jordan 9 Retro OG Space Jam 2026 was released on September 19, 2026 with a retail price of $215.
products.title: Jordan 9 Retro OG Space Jam (2026)

products.description:
The Jordan 4 Retro J Balvin Lemonade covers the AJ4 in shades of yellow that make the collaboration recognizable at a glance. Croc textured leather adds depth across the upper, so the color does more than carry the design on its own. J Balvin’s upside down smiley face appears on one heel, while Nike Air branding marks the other, continuing the uneven branding details found in his Jordan releases.

Smaller touches connect the pair to Balvin’s Colombian roots. The lace dubraes carry "JUST DO IT." and "SOLO HAZLO.", and the color story draws on the vivid scenery associated with Medellín and Colombia’s Caño Cristales river. For collectors who have followed his previous Air Jordans, this marks his move to the Jordan 4 after collaborations on earlier models. Its bright treatment gives the partnership a new look while preserving the AJ4’s familiar structure.

It is a bold pair for Balvin fans and AJ4 collectors who enjoy color and close up details. The Jordan 4 Retro J Balvin Lemonade releases September 25, 2026, with a retail price of $225.
products.title: Jordan 4 Retro J Balvin Lemonade

products.description:
The Air Jordan 4 Retro Rare Air Tour Yellow brings a vibrant, high visibility colorway into the beloved Jordan 4 silhouette, combining white, tour yellow, dark blue grey, and black into a genuinely striking presentation. The Rare Air naming ties this release to Michael Jordan's legendary competitive excellence, a phrase often associated with his singular, unmatched basketball talent. Tour yellow gives this pair significant standout presence, distinguishing it clearly from more common Jordan 4 color releases through its bold, energetic accent.

Rare Air as a concept has carried special significance within Jordan Brand's storytelling, celebrating Michael Jordan's singular basketball genius and the rarefied air of excellence he operated within throughout his career. This tour yellow execution gives the Jordan 4 genuine visual boldness, appealing to collectors who want their retro pairs to command serious attention. Fans of both Jordan Brand's storied competitive legacy and vibrant, high visibility colorways find this Rare Air release a compelling way to engage with the silhouette's continued evolution.

The Air Jordan 4 Retro Rare Air Tour Yellow was released on September 5, 2026 with a retail price of $220.
products.title: Jordan 4 Retro Rare Air Tour Yellow (2026)

products.description:
The Air Jordan 4 Retro Toro Bravo (2026) brings back one of the most recognizable non-OG colorways in the Jordan 4 archive, first introduced in 2013 during a wave of bold, lifestyle-driven releases. Dressed in fire red with white, black, and cement grey accents, the sneaker leans into high-impact color blocking that instantly stands out. The red nubuck upper gives the silhouette depth and texture, while black wings and midsole hits ground the design with contrast.

The "Toro Bravo" nickname draws from Spanish bullfighting culture, a theme Jordan Brand explored during the early 2010s when experimenting beyond traditional Bulls-inspired palettes. Unlike OG Jordan 4s tied directly to on-court moments, this pair became a streetwear favorite for its unapologetic use of color and premium materials. Over time, it’s been embraced as one of the most memorable modern-era Jordan 4s, bridging the gap between retro heritage and bold expression.

When the Air Jordan 4 Retro Toro Bravo (2026) released, it retailed for $220. With its fire red, white, black, and cement grey colorway and its status as a fan-favorite return, this release reintroduces a defining Jordan 4 look that continues to resonate across sneaker culture.
products.title: Jordan 4 Retro Toro Bravo (2026)

value.biography:
Florence Pugh (born 3 January 1996) is an English actress. Her accolades include a British Independent Film Award, in addition to nominations for an Academy Award and three BAFTA Awards.

After making her acting debut in the drama film The Falling (2014), Pugh gained praise for starring in the independent drama Lady Macbeth (2016) and the miniseries The Little Drummer Girl (2018). Her international breakthrough came in 2019 with her portrayals of professional wrestler Paige in the sports film Fighting with My Family, a despondent American woman in the horror film Midsommar, and Amy March in the period drama Little Women. For the last of these, she was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress.

Pugh has played Yelena Belova in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, starring in the films Black Widow (2021), Thunderbolts* (2025), and Spider-Man: Brand New Day (2026), as well as the Disney+ miniseries Hawkeye (2021). In her highest-grossing releases, she voiced Goldilocks in Puss in Boots: The Last Wish (2022), and portrayed Jean Tatlock in Oppenheimer (2023) and Princess Irulan in Dune: Part Two (2024); she also continued to gain praise for her performances in dramas such as We Live in Time (2024).

post.description: Finding products sold in the Netherlands and their lowest prices by keyword, then narrowing: call once, pick a category from `categories` and/or values from `filters`, and call again with `category_id`, `filters` (param -> value or values), `sort`, `min_price`, `max_price`. Take product_id into product for the per-shop offers.

category_id.description:
Pricewatch category id from `categories` (or a category filter value). Reads that category's listing, which offers its specification filters.

Provider reference: minimum 1.

filters.description: Chosen filters as Tweakers query parameters, passed through untouched: keys are a returned filter's `param`, `min_param` or `max_param`, values one of its `values[].value` (or an array of them for checkbox filters; for range filters any value on the filter's scale). Example: {"b": ["122", "1006"], "f764": "13263", "i763": "6.1"}.

max_price.description:
Highest price in whole euros (Tweakers' `pa`).

Provider reference: minimum 0; maximum 100000.

min_price.description:
Lowest price in whole euros (Tweakers' `pi`).

Provider reference: minimum 0; maximum 100000.

page.description:
Result page, 40 products per page.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 50; default 1.

query.description: Search keywords as typed in the Pricewatch search box, e.g. 'iphone 15' or 'rtx 5070'. Optional when category_id is given.

sort.description:
Result order (Tweakers' sort menu): most viewed, price low to high, price high to low, user score, newest or oldest available. Default is Tweakers' own order.

Provider reference: allowed values ["popularity", "price_asc", "price_desc", "rating", "newest", "oldest"].
